meta.title: Docs
meta.description: Get started with MCPEmails in minutes. Quick-start guide, tool reference, and example responses for Gmail and IMAP agents.

hero.lead: Connect any email account, paste one URL into an OAuth-capable MCP client and authorize. Clients without OAuth use an API key instead. Full tool reference and connection guide below.

quickstart.heading: Up and running in minutes.
quickstart.sub: No SDK required. MCPEmails speaks standard MCP over HTTP, so it drops into any MCP-compatible agent.

signup.label: Sign up & connect an inbox
signup.heading: Create your account and connect Gmail
signup.body: Sign up at mcpemails.com, then go to Dashboard → Inboxes → Connect Inbox. Pick Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail, or any IMAP inbox, then complete the OAuth flow or paste an app password. Your inbox is ready in under a minute.

apikey.label: Create an API key
apikey.heading: Generate a bearer token for your agent
apikey.body: In Dashboard → API Keys, click "Create key". Name it, select the scopes your agent needs — read:email, search:email, send:email, manage:folders, delete:email, manage:drafts, manage:contacts, and schedule:email — and copy the key. It is shown only once.

addclient.label: Add MCPEmails to your agent
addclient.heading: Paste the MCP endpoint into your client
addclient.body: Pick the tab for your client below. MCP clients with OAuth 2.0 support (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others) just paste the URL and authorize, no API key needed. Clients without OAuth, plus scripted access, use the API key from step 02.

firstcall.label: Make your first call
firstcall.heading: Ask your agent to check your inbox
firstcall.body: No copy-pasting inbox UUIDs. Your agent calls inbox_list first to discover every connected inbox and its UUID, then you ask: "Check my inbox and summarise the last 5 unread messages."

endpoint.heading: One URL, standard MCP.
endpoint.sub: All traffic goes to a single Streamable HTTP endpoint. Authenticate with a bearer token from your dashboard.
endpoint.bodyMethods: Send a JSON-RPC 2.0 request body. Supported methods: initialize, tools/list, tools/call.
endpoint.infoFormat: Response format: JSON-RPC 2.0 — successful results also carry a typed structuredContent object
endpoint.pollingBody: MCPEmails is request/response only: every result comes from a tool call your agent makes. There are no webhooks, push notifications, or server-initiated events — an incoming email never triggers an agent call on its own. To react to new mail, have your agent poll on a schedule, e.g. call email_list with unread_only: true at whatever interval your workflow needs (mind the rate limits above).

oauth.heading: Zero-config for OAuth-capable clients.
oauth.sub: MCP clients that support OAuth 2.0 (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others) connect automatically via authorization code + PKCE. No API key, no config file. Paste the URL and click Connect.
oauth.step1: Step 1: Go to claude.ai → Customize → Connectors → Add connector
oauth.step3: Step 3: Click Connect. MCPEmails opens an authorization screen
oauth.step4: Step 4: Sign in with your mcpemails account and approve access
oauth.stepDone: Done: Every tool your approved scopes allow is live. claude.ai refreshes tokens automatically
oauth.howTitle: How it works under the hood
oauth.howP1: claude.ai registers itself via RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration, so you never pre-register a client ID.
oauth.howP2: Authorization uses OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE (RFC 7636), so no client secret is ever transmitted.
oauth.howP3: Tokens are scoped to exactly the permissions you approve — read:email, search:email, send:email, manage:folders, delete:email, manage:drafts, manage:contacts, and schedule:email.
oauth.noOauthNote: Using a client without OAuth support? Create an API key in Dashboard → API Keys and pass it as a bearer token. API key and OAuth connections use the same MCP endpoint and the same tool catalogue.

tools.heading: 28 tools. Every email operation your agent needs.
tools.sub: Targeting an inbox is optional. When your key has exactly one inbox, every per-inbox tool auto-resolves it — no inbox_id needed. With multiple inboxes, pass either inbox_id (the UUID from inbox_list) or inbox (the inbox's email address). Tools are grouped by the scope that unlocks them; tools/list only returns the tools your key (or OAuth token) is scoped for. Click "Show example" to see a full request and response.

read.title: Read & search
read.desc: Discover inboxes and folders, list and read messages (singly or in batches of up to 50), and run structured, provider-agnostic searches. Read-only — never changes anything. email_search is also unlocked on its own by the narrower search:email scope.

send.title: Send & message state
send.desc: Send, reply, and forward, plus non-destructive state changes: mark messages read/unread, flag/unflag, and archive. Sends are irreversible.

folders.title: Folders & organization
folders.desc: Create, rename, and delete folders (labels on Gmail), and move messages — one at a time, in bulk, or straight from a search. Destinations accept a canonical alias (inbox, sent, drafts, trash, archive, spam), a folder/label name, or a provider-native ID.

delete.title: Delete
delete.desc: Trash or permanently expunge messages — one at a time, in bulk, or from a search. These actions are flagged as destructive to your MCP client, which handles user confirmation.

drafts.title: Drafts
drafts.desc: List, create, update, and send drafts stored in the provider's Drafts folder.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.desc: Find people by name or email with a live scan of your recent matching mail. Nothing is stored — every search reads live.

schedule.title: Scheduled send
schedule.desc: Queue an email for a future time, list pending scheduled sends, and cancel them before they go out.

tools.noParams: No parameters. Call with an empty arguments object:

inbox_list.title: List Inboxes
inbox_list.desc: Returns every inbox the current API key or OAuth token can access. Call this first to discover inbox_id values, so you never copy-paste UUIDs from the dashboard. Each result includes the email address, provider, optional service brand (icloud/yahoo/zoho/yandex/generic/fastmail), and a capabilities object describing which features that inbox supports.

email_list.title: List Messages
email_list.desc: List email summaries from a connected inbox, newest first. Supports pagination, folder selection, and unread filtering. The total field may be null when the provider cannot supply a count, or carry total_is_estimate: true on Gmail.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to list. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to discover inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.limit: Max results to return. Default 20, max 100.
params.folder: Folder to list. Default "INBOX". Other values: "SENT", "DRAFTS", "TRASH".
params.unread_only: Return only unread messages. Default false.

email_read.title: Read Email
email_read.desc: Fetch the full content of a single email by ID, including plain-text body, optional sanitized HTML, and optional attachment data.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox containing the email. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from email_list or email_search.
params.include_html: Include sanitized HTML body. Default false.
params.include_attachments: Include base64 attachment data. Default false.
params.mark_as_read: Mark message as read after fetching. Default false.

email_read_batch.title: Read Emails (batch)
email_read_batch.desc: Read up to 50 messages in a single call by their provider message IDs — ideal for triaging an inbox without one email_read round-trip per message. Returns a messages array (each in the same shape as email_read) plus a per-ID errors array, so a single bad or missing ID never fails the whole batch. When include_attachments is true, attachment data shares a single 10 MB budget across the whole call.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox containing the emails. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_ids: Provider message IDs to read, from email_list or email_search. Max 50 per call.
params.include_html: Include sanitized HTML body for each message. Default false.
params.include_attachments: Include base64 attachment data. The 10 MB total size limit is shared across all messages in the call. Default false.
params.mark_as_read: Mark each message as read after fetching. Default false.

email_search.title: Search Emails
email_search.desc: Search an inbox using structured, provider-agnostic fields — from, to, cc, subject, body, text, unread, has_attachment, flagged, since, before — combined with AND. The server translates them into the inbox's native dialect (Gmail operators, Outlook KQL/OData, Fastmail JMAP, or IMAP SEARCH), so you never need to know provider query syntax. An optional raw query is kept as an escape hatch. Provider gaps: generic IMAP ignores has_attachment, Outlook ignores flagged, and Fastmail ignores the raw query.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to search. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.from: Sender to match: email address, display name, or fragment (e.g. "alice@example.com" or "Alice").
params.to: Primary (To) recipient to match: email address, display name, or fragment.
params.cc: Carbon-copy (Cc) recipient to match: email address, display name, or fragment.
params.subject: Text to match in the subject line. Multi-word phrases are matched as-is.
params.body: Free text to find in the message body. (On Gmail this matches the whole message, not body-only.)
params.text: Free text to match anywhere in the message (headers and body).
params.unread: true = only unread messages; false = only read messages; omit for either.
params.has_attachment: true = only messages with an attachment. Not supported on generic IMAP (ignored there).
params.flagged: true = only flagged/starred messages. Not supported on Outlook/Graph (ignored there).
params.since: ISO 8601 date or datetime; return messages received on/after (>=) this instant. E.g. "2026-06-01".
params.before: ISO 8601 date or datetime; return messages received strictly before (<) this instant.
params.query: Raw provider-native query string (escape hatch). Prefer the structured fields above. Combined with them where supported; ignored on Fastmail.
params.include_folders: Restrict search to these folder names. Default: search all folders.

email_send.title: Send Email
email_send.desc: Send a new email from a connected inbox. Supports plain text, optional HTML body, CC/BCC, and file attachments (up to 10 MB total).

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to send from. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.subject: Email subject line. Max 998 characters.
params.html_body: HTML version of the body (multipart/alternative). Caller is responsible for safe HTML.
params.attachments: File attachments. Each item: '{' filename, mime_type, data (base64) '}'. Max 20 items, 10 MB total.

email_reply.title: Reply to Email
email_reply.desc: Send a reply to an existing email. Threading headers (In-Reply-To, References) are set automatically. Supports reply-all and attachments.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that contains the original message. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_id: Provider message ID of the email being replied to.
params.html_body: Optional HTML version of the reply.
params.reply_all: Reply to all original recipients (To + Cc). Default false.
params.attachments: File attachments. Same schema as email_send. Max 20 items.

folder_list.title: List Folders
folder_list.desc: List every folder (or label, on Gmail) in an inbox. Each entry has the provider-native folder ID, display name, type (folder vs label), and message counts. Use the IDs as the folder argument for email_list and as the destination for move operations.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox whose folders to list. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.

email_forward.title: Forward Email
email_forward.desc: Forward an existing message to new recipients. Your optional note is prepended above a standard forwarded-message header block and the original body. Set include_attachments to re-attach the original files. The subject is prefixed with 'Fwd:' if needed. Irreversible.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that holds the original message. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_id: Provider message ID of the email to forward, from email_list or email_search.
params.body: Optional plain-text note to prepend above the forwarded message.
params.html_body: Optional HTML version of the note (multipart/alternative).
params.include_attachments: Re-attach the original message's attachments. Files over the 10 MB budget are omitted. Default false.

email_archive.title: Archive Email
email_archive.desc: Move a message out of the Inbox to the archive. Non-destructive — the message is preserved, not deleted. On Gmail this removes the INBOX label; on IMAP/Outlook/Fastmail it moves to the Archive mailbox.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox containing the message. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from email_list or email_search.

email_flag.title: Flag or Mark Messages
email_flag.desc: Apply a read/unread/flag/unflag action to one or more messages in a single call. Use action 'read' or 'unread' to change read status, or 'flag'/'unflag' to add or remove a star/follow-up flag. Pass one message ID to update a single message, or up to 500 to update many at once. Get message IDs from email_list or email_search.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the messages. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_ids: Provider message IDs to update. Max 500 per call.
params.action: Action to apply to all messages: "read", "unread", "flag", or "unflag".

folder_create.title: Create Folder
folder_create.desc: Create a new folder (or label, on Gmail) in an inbox. Returns the provider-native folder/label ID and display name.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to create the folder/label in. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.name: Name of the new folder or label. 1–255 characters.

folder_rename.title: Rename Folder
folder_rename.desc: Rename an existing folder or label. Call folder_list first to obtain the folder_id.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the folder/label. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.

folder_delete.title: Delete Folder
folder_delete.desc: Permanently delete a folder (or label, on Gmail). Irreversible — messages inside may be lost depending on the provider. This action is flagged as destructive to your MCP client, which handles user confirmation. Call folder_list first to obtain the folder_id.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the folder/label. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.

email_move.title: Move Email
email_move.desc: Move a message to a different folder. On Gmail this adds the destination label and removes INBOX (Gmail has no separate folders). The destination accepts a canonical alias, a folder/label name, or a provider-native ID.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the message. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from email_list, email_read, or email_search.
params.destination_folder_id: Destination folder: a canonical alias (inbox, sent, drafts, trash, archive, spam), a folder/label name (e.g. 'Receipts'), or a provider-native folder ID from folder_list. Names and aliases are resolved automatically.

email_move_batch.title: Bulk Move
email_move_batch.desc: Move up to 500 messages to a destination folder in one call. Returns succeeded/failed counts plus per-message results. The destination accepts a canonical alias, a folder/label name, or a provider-native ID.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the messages. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_ids: Provider message IDs to move. Max 500 per call.
params.destination_folder_id: Destination folder: a canonical alias (inbox, sent, drafts, trash, archive, spam), a folder/label name (e.g. 'Receipts'), or a provider-native folder ID from folder_list. Names and aliases are resolved automatically.

email_search_and_move.title: Search and Move
email_search_and_move.desc: Run a structured search and move every match to a destination folder in one server-side operation — avoids stale message IDs. Uses the same provider-agnostic search fields as email_search (from, to, cc, subject, body, text, unread, has_attachment, flagged, since, before), with the same per-provider gaps; an optional raw query is kept as an escape hatch. The destination accepts a canonical alias, a folder/label name, or a provider-native ID. Capped at 500 matches per call.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to search and operate on. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.from: Sender to match: email address, display name, or fragment.
params.to: Primary (To) recipient to match: email address, display name, or fragment.
params.cc: Carbon-copy (Cc) recipient to match: email address, display name, or fragment.
params.subject: Text to match in the subject line.
params.body: Free text to find in the message body. (On Gmail this matches the whole message.)
params.text: Free text to match anywhere in the message (headers and body).
params.unread: true = only unread; false = only read; omit for either.
params.has_attachment: true = only messages with an attachment. Not supported on generic IMAP (ignored there).
params.flagged: true = only flagged/starred messages. Not supported on Outlook/Graph (ignored there).
params.since: ISO 8601 date or datetime; match messages received on/after (>=) this instant.
params.before: ISO 8601 date or datetime; match messages received strictly before (<) this instant.
params.query: Raw provider-native query string (escape hatch). Prefer the structured fields above. Ignored on Fastmail.
params.destination_folder_id: Destination folder: a canonical alias (inbox, sent, drafts, trash, archive, spam), a folder/label name (e.g. 'Receipts'), or a provider-native folder ID from folder_list. Names and aliases are resolved automatically.
params.include_folders: Restrict the search to these folder names. Default: all folders.
params.limit: Maximum number of matches to move. Default 500, max 500.

email_delete.title: Delete Email
email_delete.desc: Delete a single message. By default it moves to the provider's Trash (safer). Set permanent: true to hard-delete (bypasses Trash; may be irreversible). This action is flagged as destructive to your MCP client, which handles user confirmation. Permanent expunge is available on IMAP and Fastmail; Gmail and Outlook support trash only.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the message. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from email_list, email_read, or email_search.
params.permanent: When true, hard-delete (bypass Trash). When false or omitted, move to Trash. Default false.

email_delete_batch.title: Bulk Delete
email_delete_batch.desc: Delete up to 500 messages in one call. Defaults to Trash; set permanent: true for a hard delete. This action is flagged as destructive to your MCP client, which handles user confirmation. Returns succeeded/failed counts plus per-message results.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the messages. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_ids: Provider message IDs to delete. Max 500 per call.
params.permanent: When true, hard-delete (bypass Trash). When false or omitted, move to Trash. Default false.

email_search_and_delete.title: Search and Delete
email_search_and_delete.desc: Run a structured search and delete every match in one server-side operation — avoids stale message IDs. Uses the same provider-agnostic search fields as email_search (from, to, cc, subject, body, text, unread, has_attachment, flagged, since, before), with the same per-provider gaps; an optional raw query is kept as an escape hatch. Defaults to Trash; set permanent: true for a hard delete. This action is flagged as destructive to your MCP client, which handles user confirmation. Capped at 500 matches per call.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to search and operate on. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.from: Sender to match: email address, display name, or fragment.
params.to: Primary (To) recipient to match: email address, display name, or fragment.
params.cc: Carbon-copy (Cc) recipient to match: email address, display name, or fragment.
params.subject: Text to match in the subject line.
params.body: Free text to find in the message body. (On Gmail this matches the whole message.)
params.text: Free text to match anywhere in the message (headers and body).
params.unread: true = only unread; false = only read; omit for either.
params.has_attachment: true = only messages with an attachment. Not supported on generic IMAP (ignored there).
params.flagged: true = only flagged/starred messages. Not supported on Outlook/Graph (ignored there).
params.since: ISO 8601 date or datetime; match messages received on/after (>=) this instant.
params.before: ISO 8601 date or datetime; match messages received strictly before (<) this instant.
params.query: Raw provider-native query string (escape hatch). Prefer the structured fields above. Ignored on Fastmail.
params.permanent: When true, hard-delete matches (bypass Trash). When false or omitted, move to Trash. Default false.
params.include_folders: Restrict the search to these folder names. Default: all folders.
params.limit: Maximum number of matches to delete. Default 500, max 500.

draft_list.title: List Drafts
draft_list.desc: Return drafts saved in the inbox's Drafts folder. Each result includes the draft_id, subject, recipients, and created timestamp. Use the draft_id with draft_update or draft_send.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox whose drafts to list. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.limit: Maximum number of drafts to return. Default 20, max 50.

draft_create.title: Create Draft
draft_create.desc: Save a new draft in the inbox's Drafts folder without sending it. Returns a draft_id for draft_update or draft_send. Subject and body are required; recipients are optional (drafts may be incomplete).

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to save the draft in. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.subject: Draft subject line.

draft_update.title: Update Draft
draft_update.desc: Replace the content of an existing draft. All supplied fields overwrite the stored draft. Call draft_list to obtain draft_id values. On IMAP-backed inboxes (anything other than Gmail/Outlook) the underlying message is rewritten, so this returns a NEW draft_id that replaces the one you passed in — adopt it for any further draft_update/draft_send and discard the old one. Gmail and Outlook keep a stable draft_id.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the draft. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.draft_id: Provider draft ID from the most recent draft_create, draft_update, or draft_list. On IMAP inboxes it changes after every update, so always use the latest one.
params.subject: Updated subject line.

draft_send.title: Send Draft
draft_send.desc: Send a previously saved draft. The draft is removed from the Drafts folder after sending. Irreversible. Always pass the most recent draft_id (from draft_create, the latest draft_update, or draft_list): on IMAP-backed inboxes the id changes on every update, and a stale id fails with a not-found error.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that contains the draft. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.draft_id: Provider draft ID from the most recent draft_create, draft_update, or draft_list. On IMAP inboxes it changes after every update, so always use the latest one.

contact_search.title: Search Contacts
contact_search.desc: Find correspondents by name or email with a live scan of your mailbox — there is no stored contact list. Each call scans a recent window of matching mail and returns the people who match, sorted by most-recently-contacted, each with display name, email, matched-message count, and last-contacted timestamp. Counts reflect matched messages in that window, not your full history, and nothing is stored between calls.

params.query: Name or email fragment, matched case-insensitively against display name and address. At least 1 character.
params.inbox_id: Optional. Restrict the live scan to one inbox. Omit to scan the inboxes the key can access (a bounded number).
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to restrict to, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.limit: Maximum number of contacts to return. Default 20, max 50.

schedule_create.title: Schedule Send
schedule_create.desc: Queue an email to be sent at a future time. Recipients and body are validated immediately; if validation fails it is not queued. The dispatcher runs every minute, so actual delivery may be up to 60 seconds after send_at. Use schedule_list and schedule_cancel to manage pending sends.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to send from. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.subject: Email subject line. Max 998 characters.
params.send_at: ISO 8601 datetime with timezone at which to send. Must be in the future, e.g. "2026-06-02T09:00:00Z".
params.html_body: Optional HTML version of the body.
params.attachments: File attachments. Same schema as email_send. Max 20 items, 10 MB total.

schedule_list.title: List Scheduled Sends
schedule_list.desc: List pending scheduled sends for the workspace (status pending or sending), earliest first. Optionally filter by inbox. Use schedule_cancel to cancel one before it dispatches.

params.inbox_id: Optional. Restrict results to scheduled sends for one inbox.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to restrict to, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.limit: Maximum number of results. Default 20, max 100.

schedule_cancel.title: Cancel Scheduled Send
schedule_cancel.desc: Cancel a pending scheduled send so the dispatcher skips it. Only sends still in 'pending' state can be cancelled — once 'sending', 'sent', or 'error' they cannot. Use schedule_list to find the scheduled_send_id.

params.scheduled_send_id: UUID of the scheduled send to cancel.

errors.heading: Error codes & retry guidance.
errors.sub: Auth, scope, and rate limit failures return a JSON-RPC error object with a numeric code. Tool execution failures (inbox not found, provider error, etc.) return a normal result with isError: true and a human-readable message in content[0].text.

rows.auth: Missing, malformed, revoked, or expired API key. Also returned when the API key lacks the required scope for the called tool.
rows.method: Unknown JSON-RPC method (e.g. calling a method other than initialize, tools/list, tools/call)
rows.param: Unknown tool name, or missing / invalid parameter in tools/call
rows.rate: Per-key rate limit or plan daily quota exceeded. Check data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" vs "quota_exceeded". Check data.retry_after (seconds) before retrying.
rows.tool: Tool executed but encountered an error (inbox not found, message not found, provider auth failure, invalid recipient, attachment too large, provider 5xx). The error description is in content[0].text.

rateLimits.heading: Rate limits & quotas.
rateLimits.perKeyBody: Enforced per API key regardless of plan. When exceeded, the server returns error code -32029 with data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" and a data.retry_after field (seconds). Respect that value before retrying.
rateLimits.planHeading: Free 60 / min · Solo 300 / min · Team 1,000 / min
rateLimits.planBody: Usage is unlimited; this is a per-workspace fair-use burst limit (aggregated across all your API keys). When exceeded, calls return data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" with data.window: "per_minute" and a data.retry_after countdown (seconds). Upgrade your plan for a higher ceiling.
rateLimits.retryHeading: Always honour retry_after; never retry sends blindly
rateLimits.retryBody: For rate_limit_exceeded errors, wait data.retry_after seconds before retrying. Use exponential backoff for provider_error. Do not auto-retry email_send on provider_error, since the message may have already been accepted by the provider.

cta.sub: Start on the Free plan: unlimited, no card required. Upgrade to Solo or Team for higher burst limits and team features.

meta.title: Provider Support
meta.description: See which email providers MCPEmails supports and which features are available per provider: Gmail, Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, and Generic IMAP.

hero.heading: What works, per provider.
hero.lead: MCPEmails connects Gmail, Fastmail, and any IMAP inbox (iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, generic). Not every provider exposes the same APIs — this table shows exactly what each one supports today.

legend.imapNote: Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, and Generic IMAP all connect over the same IMAP/SMTP transport (Fastmail and iCloud use an app-specific password) and share an identical feature set, including IMAP search syntax. The columns are shown separately for clarity.

notes.gmail: Gmail — folders vs labels: Gmail uses a flat label system rather than hierarchical folders. "Move" is implemented as label add/remove. Native copy is not available via the Gmail REST API.
notes.permanentDelete: Permanent delete: Gmail moves to Trash when you delete — permanent expunge is not exposed by their APIs. IMAP providers (Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, Generic) support both trash and hard expunge.
notes.contacts_db: Contact search (live scan): All providers support contact_search, which finds matching correspondents with a live, header-only scan of a recent window of your matching mail. There is no contacts table — nothing is stored between calls, and counts reflect only matched messages in the scanned window.
notes.scheduling: Scheduling: Supported for all providers via a server-side scheduled_sends queue. Use schedule_create, schedule_list, and schedule_cancel. Delivery uses each provider's existing send path — no provider-native scheduling API is required.
